subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and which parts should instead live in plugins, SDK seams, or ClawHub?
rationale: The safety goal fits current priorities, but implementing it touches storage policy, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, Doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-vs-plugin boundaries that require maintainer intent before a safe fix PR can be queued.

options.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
options.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific audit/review staging classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Core would own temp artifact classes, provenance storage, and cleanup/janitor policy for all first-class OpenClaw-created temp artifacts.

options.title: Keep only concrete bug fixes
options.body: Decline the broad core default for now and track narrower bugs such as backup/temp cleanup or runtime path drift independently.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific audit/review staging classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combination of recent temp/Doctor/agent-surface history and prior product-scope decision context for the adjacent review-staged request.
